deskyard computer create: create a computer (admin)

Usage: deskyard [-c COMPUTER] computer create NAME --image REF [OPTIONS]

Creates a computer from an image and starts it, printing the progress (pulling
the image, starting the desktop) on stderr until it is ready; Ctrl-C stops
following, not the creation. Its files are in home/NAME/ in the server's data
folder; a folder left by an earlier computer of that name is reused.
Administrators have access to every computer; --grant gives it to other
accounts.

Arguments:
  NAME       string      required  computer name (2–32 lowercase letters, digits and -)

Options:
  --image REF          image reference (required), e.g.
                       ghcr.io/zefhemel/deskyard-debian-xfce:latest
  --memory BYTES       memory limit in bytes, or with K, M, G or T (4G);
                       default no limit
  --cpus N             CPU limit, e.g. 2 or 1.5; default no limit
  --grant USER[=observe] give an account full access, or observe-only with
                       =observe (repeatable)
  --volume NAME[:ro]   mount a volume at /share/NAME, read-only with :ro
                       (repeatable)
  --server NAME        the server to manage (see `deskyard server list`);
                       default: the server -c SERVER/COMPUTER names, else the
                       default server

Prints: the new computer's URL once it is ready; progress on stderr

Examples:
  deskyard computer create bob --image ghcr.io/zefhemel/deskyard-debian-xfce:latest --memory 4G --cpus 2 --grant bob
  deskyard computer create lab --image ghcr.io/zefhemel/deskyard-debian-xfce:latest --volume photos:ro

Where: on this machine, talking to the server
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage error; the server's refusal (403 for what your account may not do) is an error
